content:
When you throw two standard six-sided dice, the possible outcomes for each die range from 1 to 6. The sum of the numbers shown on the two dice can therefore range from 2 (if both dice show a 1) to 12 (if both dice show a 6).

Since the maximum sum you can achieve with two six-sided dice is 12, it is impossible to get a sum of 13. Therefore, the probability of rolling a sum of 13 with two standard six-sided dice is 0.
